options.idea: A printmaker reveals the first complete tide-map relief print after several spoiled sheets. One hand lifts the corner, the other keeps the inked block steady. The clean wet impression, spoiled edge fragments and restrained relieved smile connect effort to result in a coastal print workshop.

A greenhouse caretaker uses an upturned ceramic bowl as a dry shelf for a waterlogged seed packet while her other hand redirects a storm leak with a bent brass gutter. The two hands protect a small hopeful future amid wet leaves and dawn light.

A potter pauses at a window with an experimental perforated bowl. One hand holds it over a basin while the other catches the last ribbon of water on a fingertip. A proud almost-laugh acknowledges that a failed vessel has become a useful strainer, with clay slurry and ordinary workshop tools making the transformation legible.

A theatre scenery maker repairs a torn translucent paper moon in a backstage workshop. One hand anchors the patch, the other smooths rice paste. The lamp shines through the mended seam and her absorbed, softly amused look makes care visible before the coming performance.

A bookbinder presses a newly stitched fold of a rain-damaged coastal atlas on a wooden bench. One hand flattens the fold, the other draws linen thread taut. Dried tide stains and a small restored compass rose hold the tension between damage and persistence.

benchmark_authorial_capture_choice: fixed-device self-portrait; not a requester-owned camera lock
reference_observation: Short dark bob and wispy bangs, visible facial proportions; no inferred identity, age or biography.
whole_image_criteria: Readable action and present material result; distinctive subject presence; emotional credibility; hands serve the event; one clear visual hierarchy.
